source.title: LSSF: Safety Alignment for Large Language Models through Low-Rank Safety Subspace Fusion
source.authors: Guang-Hao Zhou; Panjia Qiu; Cen Chen; Hong-Yu Li; Mingyuan Chu; Xin Zhang; Jun Zhou

record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-request refusal after fine-tuning and tests whether adding low-rank safety components restores refusal; it does not reproduce the original studies' first-token KL or prefilling tests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports refusal rates after downstream fine-tuning and after its low-rank safety-component addition. It also describes robustness experiments varying harmful or safe data proportions in Figure 6, but gives no exact plotted values in the text. Values cited from prior work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Section 4.1.2 tests whether a low-rank projection of the safety vector carries the full vector's safety effect (V5), using activation-SVD projection rather than the originals' methods. The NA-SFT tables show refusal collapse after fine-tuning that apparently mixes in 500 harmful examples, which bears on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that safety lies in a low-rank subspace that stays largely unchanged through fine-tuning and is isolated from general-capability directions. Adding the safety vector's low-rank principal components restores refusal with little downstream-task cost, outperforming RESTA, Lisa and VLGuard on utility.
record.recipe_differences: This study proposes post-hoc low-rank projection and safety-component fusion; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or first-token KL/prefill recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported refusal rate depends on the evaluation dataset and downstream task. The authors also report that varying the singular-value entropy threshold and singular-vector weights changes safety and utility, and that encoding density differs by layer and matrix.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The main NA-SFT tables lack matched pre-fine-tuning refusal rates and do not specify the training-data composition for each condition, limiting conclusions about whether fine-tuning caused a safety decline. The study reports no uncertainty estimates. Figure 6's safe/harmful data-mixture outcomes are described qualitatively without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figure 6's mixture-ratio outcomes were not entered as rows because exact values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: No dose-response. NA-SFT harmful-sample count is inferred (likely 500 in 50K) rather than stated per table. The 500-example harmful SFT used to build the unsafe model reports no refusal rate.
No benign-only fine-tuning condition is isolated; NA-SFT appears to include harmful samples.
Not tested; no prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
The absolute rank or parameter count retained in the main results (η=0.9) is not reported.

missing.what: Refusal rate vs singular-value entropy threshold η (0.5–0.9); safety improves with η and nears 1.0 above 0.8
Refusal vs left-singular-vector weight α at η=0.5; near safety-model level when α>2.5
Retained rank ratio vs η per matrix and layer (up to ~0.5; v_proj vs q_proj differ >30% at layer 15)
General-capability preservation of low-rank components vs the full safety vector (BBH 68.52 vs 20.03; IFEval 81.88 vs 35.01)

record.verdict_notes: Table text extraction scrambles column order. Values here follow the Table 1 pattern checked against Table 8 (Ours on AG's News for Qwen-7B: HarmfulQA 0.93, CATQA 0.98); the HarmfulQA/CATQA assignment in Tables 2–3 is inferred the same way. Llama NA-SFT HarmfulQA is 0.49 in all three tables. The NA-SFT data mix is not stated directly; D.1 and 4.1.1 imply 500 harmful samples were mixed in. The safety vector itself comes from a 500-example harmful SFT whose refusal is never reported. Tables 1–3 LSSF rows are the paper's method, but they directly test whether low-rank components carry safety, so they are kept for V5.

versions.untested_parts: No matched pre-fine-tuning refusal rate is reported, and the main tables do not state the harmful-example count or composition for each NA-SFT condition; the study does not establish a dose-response for a few to a few hundred examples.
No matched pre-fine-tuning refusal rate is reported, and the main tables do not isolate benign-only training data from any mixed data.
Per-token KL divergence by response position is not measured.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass is tested.
The study tests adding low-rank safety components, but does not report the retained rank or parameter count for the behavioral results, or compare against a systematic range of ranks.
The study does not test whether a data or training-objective mechanism produces first-token shallowness.
The study does not train safety to be distributed across later response tokens or test whether such training holds up.
